Its decisions have been carried into [requirements.md](requirements.md), the specs ([S-A](specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md), [S-B](specs/S-B-rule-engine-research.md), [S-C](specs/S-C-rule-engine-spec.md)) and [QA.csv](QA.csv).
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Purpose
8	
9	The agent watches signals about a person's surroundings and body, decides on its own when something is worth knowing, and responds. It speaks rarely, says what changed and why it matters to *this* person, and offers one thing to do. Restraint matters as much as detection.
10	
11	The design is described at two scopes that share **one set of layers**:
12	
13	- **Full scope**, the ultimate goal: many signals (air, pollen, weather, heart rate, sleep, movement, the home) and many responses (a message, an alarm, a call for help, adjusting the home), with settings that learn.
14	- **Demo scope**, what we build now: air quality (PM2.5) in five cities, notifications only, every requirement in the brief met.
15	
16	The demo isn't a separate, simpler design. It's the full design with some layers reduced to a single rule or left out. Sections 2–4 give the big picture. Sections 5–9 walk through the layers. Section 10 follows one night end to end, and section 11 records the decisions.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 2. The layers at full scope
21	
22	Eighteen layers in five planes. Each answers **one question** for **one unit of work**: a data source, a signal stream, a person, a story (episode) or a response.
23	
24	```
25	 FULL SCOPE: the ultimate goal
26	 +================================================================================+
27	 | PLANE        UNIT OF WORK   LAYER          THE ONE QUESTION IT ANSWERS         |
28	 +================================================================================+
29	 | SENSE        per source     S1 INGEST      Did we get the data?                 |
30	 |                             S2 VALIDATE    Can we trust it?                     |
31	 |                             S3 RESOLVE     Whose is it, where does it apply,    |
32	 |                                            and may we use it? (consent)         |
33	 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
34	 | UNDERSTAND   per stream     U1 LEARN       What is normal for this stream,      |
35	 |                                            here, at this time?                  |
36	 |                             U2 SCORE       How unusual? How harmful?            |
37	 |              per person     U3 FUSE        What does it mean alongside their    |
38	 |                                            other signals and context?           |
39	 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
40	 | DECIDE       per story      D1 TRIGGER     Is this an event for this person,    |
41	 |                                            and what kind?                       |
42	 |                             D2 EPISODE     A new story, or the same story?      |
43	 |                             D3 WORTH IT    Is there anything new in this story? |
44	 |                             D4 PACE        Too soon since this story last spoke?|
45	 |              per person     D5 ARBITRATE   Which candidate wins right now?      |
46	 |                             D6 RESPOND     Tell them, set an alarm, call for    |
47	 |                                            help, or adjust the home?            |
48	 |                             D7 BUDGET      Can we afford their attention today? |
49	 |                             D8 TIMING      Is now the right moment?             |
50	 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
51	 | ACT          per response   A1 COMPOSE     How do we say it?                    |
52	 |                             A2 DELIVER     Did it reach them / did it happen?   |
53	 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
54	 | LEARN        per person     L1 FEEDBACK    How did they respond?                |
55	 |                             L2 ADAPT       Should their settings change?        |
56	 +================================================================================+
57	 | CROSS-CUTTING  RECORD   every answer, including "stay quiet"                    |
58	 |                REPLAY   any past hour, exactly as it was known then             |
59	 |                GUARD    consent, and safety limits on high-stakes actions       |
60	 |                OPERATE  is the pipeline itself healthy (freshness, failures)?   |
61	 +================================================================================+
62	```
63	
64	Three structural choices shape everything else:
65	
66	- **Station work is shared, person work is not.** SENSE and UNDERSTAND produce facts about a place that are the same for everyone: how unusual the air is, and how harmful. Everything personal (sensitivity, schedule, history) starts at D1. A person's settings never change a station's scores.
67	- **DECIDE has two halves.** D1–D4 judge **one story at a time** ("Delhi's air is getting worse"). D5–D8 judge **the person as a whole**, across every story competing for their attention: Delhi air, high pollen, an odd heart-rate reading. Keeping those apart is what stops alert fatigue once there are many signals.
68	- **What comes before when.** D6 RESPOND comes before D7 BUDGET and D8 TIMING, because the kind of response changes both. A call for help ignores quiet hours and is never "over budget". A routine heads-up respects both.
69	
70	What full scope looks like in practice (illustrative):
71	
72	```
73	  Fusion: three ordinary-looking signals become one clear message
74	
75	   air (U2):    PM2.5 above normal, Unhealthy ----+
76	   body (U2):   heart rate 15% above their usual -+--> U3 FUSE: "exerting in bad air"
77	   motion (S1): running for the last 20 min ------+          |
78	                                                             v
79	                       D1..D8 --> A1: "The air's turned unhealthy and your heart rate's
80	                                       up. Maybe walk the rest of the way home."
81	
82	  High-stakes response: GUARD sits in front of every irreversible action
83	
84	   asthma profile + Hazardous air + no reply to 2 messages in 30 min
85	       --> D6 RESPOND proposes "SOS to emergency contact"
86	       --> GUARD: is consent on file? Is the action rate-limited? Does it need a
87	                  one-tap confirmation, or a timeout?
88	       --> A2 DELIVER: send it, and record the receipt
89	```
90	
91	---
92	
93	## 3. The layers at demo scope
94	
95	The same eighteen layers. Each one is **REAL** (built properly), a **STUB** (a single rule, named in code and in every decision trace, so the seam is visible) or **NONE** (left out, because nothing needs it yet).
96	
97	```
98	 DEMO SCOPE: air quality, 5 cities, notifications only
99	 +==================================================================================+
100	 | LAYER          STATUS  WHAT IT IS IN THE DEMO                          BRIEF      |
101	 +==================================================================================+
102	 | S1 INGEST      REAL    OpenAQ hourly, trailing 24h window, backfill   B1         |
103	 | S2 VALIDATE    REAL    invalid / low coverage / stuck / glitch checks B2d        |
104	 | S3 RESOLVE     STUB    hardcoded user -> one station; no consent step  B5         |
105	 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
106	 | U1 LEARN       REAL    14-day hour-of-day baseline per station         B2e, B5    |
107	 | U2 SCORE       REAL    unusual: z, EWMA, CUSUM, slope                  B2e        |
108	 |                        harmful: NowCast -> EPA band                               |
109	 | U3 FUSE        NONE    one signal, so nothing to fuse                  -          |
110	 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
111	 | D1 TRIGGER     REAL    spike / climb / elevated / clearing / floor,    B2a-c, B5  |
112	 |                        scaled by the person's sensitivity                         |
113	 | D2 EPISODE     REAL    lifecycle, hysteresis, flap guard, timeout      B3         |
114	 | D3 WORTH IT    REAL    relevance floor, one-band escalation,           B3         |
115	 |                        "cleared" only after a bad period                          |
116	 | D4 PACE        REAL    6h gap, doubling within a story                 BX1        |
117	 | D5 ARBITRATE   STUB    one message per person per hour, by priority    B3         |
118	 | D6 RESPOND     STUB    always "notify"                                 -          |
119	 | D7 BUDGET      STUB    at most 3 non-severe messages per person a day  B3         |
120	 | D8 TIMING      REAL    quiet hours (hold and release), morning check-in -         |
121	 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
122	 | A1 COMPOSE     REAL    LLM from verified facts, template fallback      B4         |
123	 | A2 DELIVER     STUB    "delivered" = visible in the feed and export    S5         |
124	 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
125	 | L1 FEEDBACK    REAL*   records acted / dismissed / not useful          -          |
126	 | L2 ADAPT       STUB    no changes; rules are versioned for later       -          |
127	 +==================================================================================+
128	 | RECORD  REAL   decision log for every person x hour, with reasons      B6         |
129	 | REPLAY  REAL   replay harness on as-known data, caught vs missed       BX2        |
130	 | GUARD   NONE   no high-stakes actions yet                              -          |
131	 | OPERATE REAL*  ingestion runs: freshness, failures, rate limits        -          |
132	 +==================================================================================+
133	   REAL* = real but minimal.   11 real · 6 stubs · 1 none, plus 3 of 4 cross-cutting.
134	```
135	
136	How each stub or empty layer grows into its full form:
137	
138	| Layer | Demo | Full scope |
139	|---|---|---|
140	| S3 RESOLVE | a fixed person-to-station mapping | identity, devices, locations, consent per signal |
141	| U3 FUSE | none | combines streams and context into one meaning ("exerting in bad air") |
142	| D5 ARBITRATE | one message per hour, by a fixed priority | ranks competing stories by urgency and relevance |
143	| D6 RESPOND | always notify | chooses between a message, an alarm, an SOS, a home action, with escalation |
144	| D7 BUDGET | 3 non-severe a day | an attention budget shared by all signals, tuned per person |
145	| A2 DELIVER | written to the feed | push, email, SMS, device APIs, with retries and receipts |
146	| L2 ADAPT | none; rules are versioned | proposes a new "learned" rules version, bounded by GUARD and reversible |
147	| GUARD | none | consent, confirmations and rate limits before any irreversible action |
148	
149	A stub costs one rule, but it puts the layer in the code and in every trace (`ARBITRATE: 1 candidate, kept`). Later, the layer gets filled in, not invented. Three stubs are needed even in the demo. A check-in and an episode message can land in the same hour (ARBITRATE). A jumpy day with back-to-back episodes could otherwise stack up messages (BUDGET). And the brief asks for a notification history (DELIVER).
150	
151	---
152	
153	## 4. Two clocks drive it
154	
155	Most work happens when new data arrives. Some must happen when **no** data arrives: noticing a silent sensor, releasing messages held overnight, running the morning check-in. So every hour, every person gets a decision, whichever clock fired.
156	
157	```
158	   OpenAQ
159	     |   every hour at :20, fetch the last 24h per sensor
160	     v
161	  [S1..S2] --new or revised hours--> [U1..U2] --scores--> [D1..D8] --> [A1..A2] --> feed
162	                                                              ^
163	   CLOCK -----------------------------------------------------+
164	     every hour, plus each person's check-in time and the end of their quiet hours:
165	       - marks sensors without fresh data as NO_DATA
166	       - releases messages held overnight
167	       - runs the morning check-in
168	```
169	
170	---
171	
172	## 5. Sense: getting data we can trust
173	
174	**S1 INGEST.** Every hour, for each tracked sensor, fetch the **last 24 hours** and store anything new. Data usually arrives 0.5–2.5 hours late, and sometimes much later. The overlapping window picks up late readings, and the newly filled hours are evaluated as if they had arrived on time. Readings are never overwritten. A changed value is stored as a new version with the time we received it, so we can always ask "what did we know at 3am?". On first run, up to 90 days are backfilled so a baseline exists from day one.
175	
176	**S2 VALIDATE.** OpenAQ doesn't flag bad readings, so we do.
177	
178	| Check | Rule | Example from the real data |
179	|---|---|---|
180	| Invalid | below 0 or above 1000 µg/m³ | Sydney low-cost sensors: about a third of hours ≤ 0 (not tracked) |
181	| Low coverage | the hour is less than 75% complete | — |
182	| Stuck | the same value for 6+ hours | — |
183	| Glitch | 3× higher than both neighbours and +20 µg/m³ | Mumbai: 75 → **980** → 90 in three hours; 8 such hours in 58 days, none flagged by OpenAQ |
184	
185	Excluded readings stay visible as evidence. They just don't count. The newest hour can't be glitch-checked until the next one arrives. That costs nothing, because a spike needs two hours of confirmation anyway.
186	
187	**S3 RESOLVE.** In the demo, each person follows exactly one station. At full scope this layer answers whose device a reading came from, which places a person cares about, and whether we have consent to use each signal.
188	
189	---
190	
191	## 6. Understand: what is normal, and what is harmful
192	
193	**U1 LEARN.** For each station and each hour of the day, the agent learns what's normal from the last 14 days. It works on a log scale, so a doubling means the same thing in Helsinki and in Delhi. It uses the median and median absolute deviation, so last week's smoke doesn't distort "normal". Hours with little history borrow from the station's all-day pattern, and a station needs 72 hours of clean history before it can judge anything. Each station also gets a **typical band**: the official air quality category of its usual level.
194	
195	```
196	  what "normal" looks like (90-day medians, µg/m³)
197	
198	   Helsinki     4.2  |##                                     typical: Good
199	   Los Angeles 10.0  |#####                                  typical: Moderate
200	   Bengaluru   20.7  |##########                             typical: Moderate
201	   Dubai       41.0  |####################                   typical: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups
202	   Delhi       45.9  |######################                 typical: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups
203	                     +----+----+----+----+----+
204	                     0   10   20   30   40   50
205	```
206	
207	**U2 SCORE.** Two different questions get two different answers, and neither depends on who is asking.
208	- **How unusual?** How far the latest hour sits from normal for that hour of day (z). That comes with a smoothed version (EWMA), a running total of excess (CUSUM) and the direction of the last 6 hours (slope).
209	- **How harmful?** The official US EPA category of the hourly-weighted average (NowCast): Good, Moderate, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, Hazardous. Same scale everywhere.
210	
211	A message needs the right combination of the two:
212	
213	```
214	                              Is it HARMFUL? (EPA band, same scale everywhere)
215	                               no (Good)                   yes (Moderate or worse)
216	                         +---------------------------+---------------------------------+
217	   Is it UNUSUAL         | Stay quiet.               | TELL THEM.                       |
218	   for this place?   yes | "Helsinki went 3 -> 5."   | "Worse than a normal Delhi       |
219	   (learned per          | Odd, but harmless.        |  morning, and unhealthy."        |
220	   station, per hour)    |                           |                                  |
221	                         +---------------------------+---------------------------------+
222	                      no | Nothing to say.           | Mostly quiet. Delhi sits in      |
223	                         |                           | "unhealthy for sensitive groups" |
224	                         |                           | for weeks; saying so hourly is   |
225	                         |                           | noise. Two exceptions:           |
226	                         |                           | - crossing UP into the person's  |
227	                         |                           |   alert band                     |
228	                         |                           | - the morning check-in, when     |
229	                         |                           |   today is worse than usual      |
230	                         +---------------------------+---------------------------------+
231	```
232	
233	That's how a clean city gets a lower bar for "unusual" without anyone hearing about harmless changes.
234	
235	**U3 FUSE** is not in the demo. At full scope it combines a person's streams and context into one meaning before anything is decided.
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 7. Decide: from a score to a message, with restraint
240	
241	### 7.1 D1 TRIGGER: is it an event, and what kind?
242	
243	```
244	  how far above normal (z)
245	   ^
246	   |        SPIKE                 CLIMB                    ELEVATED
247	   |          |                       ___/
248	   |          |\                  ___/                   ______________
249	   |          | \            ____/                  ____/
250	   |   _______|  \______  __/                    __/
251	   |
252	   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------> hours
253	      a sharp jump vs the      rising, hour after        stuck above normal
254	      last few hours           hour                      for many hours, but
255	                                                         not rising
256	      far above normal in      smoothed level above      running total of excess
257	      2 of the last 3 hours    the bar for 3 hours       crosses the bar; resets
258	                               AND the 6h slope is up    once it fires
259	
260	      CLEARING   an open episode has 4 calm hours AND is back to the station's typical band
261	      FLOOR      crossing UP into the person's alert band, whatever is "normal" there
262	```
263	
264	- **One label per event**, by priority: spike, then climb, then elevated. The label drives the wording ("jumped sharply", "getting worse since 2am", "stuck above normal all day").
265	- **Every way of getting worse is covered.** Air goes up fast (spike), keeps rising (climb), or sits high and flat (elevated). Falling-but-still-high isn't a new event. It's the same story continuing.
266	- **Elevated exists to catch what the others miss.** These are slow build-ups that never look dramatic in any single hour.
267	- **The person's sensitivity scales every bar.** Sensitive people get bars 25% lower; people who want fewer messages get bars 25% higher. Station scores are unchanged; only the bar moves.
268	
269	### 7.2 D2 EPISODE: one bad period is one story
270	
271	```
272	                 event fires AND the air is at least Moderate
273	     NORMAL  --------------------------------------------->  ACTIVE  <-----+
274	       ^                                                        |          |
275	       |                                            a calm hour |          | event again, or
276	       |  6h pass after close                                   v          | a non-calm hour
277	       |                                                   RECOVERING -----+
278	     CLOSED  <------------- 4 calm hours in a row --------------+
279	       |   ^
280	       |   +---- 24h with NO DATA: close quietly, no message (NO_DATA_TIMEOUT)
281	       |
282	       +-- event within 6h of closing --> the SAME episode reopens (no "it's getting bad" again)
283	
284	     NO DATA (under 24h): the episode is frozen. Nothing opens, closes or notifies.
285	                          When data returns, the missing hours are replayed in order.
286	```
287	
288	### 7.3 D3–D8: restraint, story first, then person
289	
290	```
291	   candidate (opened / got worse / cleared / check-in)
292	        |
293	   ---- per STORY -------------------------------------------------------------------
294	        v
295	   [D3 WORTH IT]   anything NEW in this story?
296	        |            opened: yes, if the air is at least Moderate
297	        |            got worse: only if a full band worse than last told
298	        |            cleared: only after a genuinely bad period
299	        |                     (12h or longer, or peaked above both USG and the usual band)
300	        |   no --> suppressed  BELOW_RELEVANCE / DEDUP_SAME_BAND / RECOVERY_NOT_WORTH_SAYING
301	        v
302	   [D4 PACE]       too soon since this story last spoke?   6h, then 12h, then 24h
303	        |   no --> suppressed  COOLDOWN                  (severe air skips the wait)
304	        |
305	   ---- per PERSON ------------------------------------------------------------------
306	        v
307	   [D5 ARBITRATE]  several candidates this hour? keep one:
308	        |            got worse > opened > cleared > check-in
309	        |   lost --> suppressed  ARBITRATED_OUT
310	        v
311	   [D6 RESPOND]    which response?   (demo: always notify)
312	        v
313	   [D7 BUDGET]     over today's attention budget?   3 non-severe a day
314	        |   yes --> suppressed  DAILY_BUDGET          (severe air is never over budget)
315	        v
316	   [D8 TIMING]     a good moment?
317	        |            quiet hours (22:00-07:00 by default) hold messages until morning,
318	        |            unless the air is Very Unhealthy or worse
319	        |            the morning check-in is an explicit "talk to me now": it wins over
320	        |            quiet hours and absorbs any held messages into one
321	        |   no --> held  QUIET_HOURS_HELD   (released later as ONE combined message)
322	        v
323	   [A1 COMPOSE] -> [A2 DELIVER] -> sent
324	```
325	
326	- **PACE and BUDGET are different questions.** PACE asks "too soon *in this story*?" and resets when the story ends. BUDGET asks "how much of *this person's* attention have we spent today, across every story?" With one signal they rarely disagree. With several, three well-paced stories can still add up to too much.
327	- **Held messages are never just dropped.** At release, everything held for a person becomes **one** message about the current state. It's re-checked against D3–D7 at that moment. If the story ended overnight without ever being told, nothing is sent.
328	- **The check-in is not a daily report.** At the person's chosen time, it looks at the last 8 hours. It speaks only if the air is at least Moderate and worse than usual for that time, and nothing was sent in the last 6 hours.
329	
330	**How the numbers were chosen.** Every bar and waiting time above was tuned by replaying 90 days of real data from all five cities. On the earlier version of these rules, a default person got about 1.5 messages a week in Helsinki, 2–2.5 in Los Angeles, Bengaluru and Dubai, and 3.5 in Delhi during its build-up season. The replay harness re-measures this whenever a rule changes.
331	
332	---
333	
334	## 8. Act: saying it well
335	
336	**A1 COMPOSE.** The decision layers hand over **verified facts**, never raw data:
337	
338	```
339	  { kind: "got worse",  city: "Delhi",  local time: 08:00,
340	    now: 142 µg/m³, Very Unhealthy,      usual for 8am: 48, USG,
341	    story: since 2am, 6 hours, peak 151 at 6am,
342	    history: "worst since 13 Oct", "third bad morning this week",
343	    person: Arjun, runs at 06:30,
344	    action options: skip the outdoor run | keep windows closed | wear an N95 outside }
345	```
346	
347	- An LLM writes one or two sentences from these facts. A validator then checks the result: short enough for a phone notification, includes exactly one of the offered actions, and cites no number or date that isn't in the facts.
348	- If the LLM fails the check or isn't available, a template writes the message from the same facts.
349	- Past context is always included for climb, spike and clearing messages ("since 2am", "worst since Tuesday", "back to normal after two rough days"). It's never a bare status like "AQI is now 142".
350	
351	**A2 DELIVER.** In the demo, a message is "delivered" when it appears in the person's feed and in the exported history. Real channels come at full scope.
352	
353	---
354	
355	## 9. Learn, and what runs across everything
356	
357	- **L1 FEEDBACK.** A person can mark a message as acted on, dismissed or not useful. In the demo, this is stored and shown next to the decision, and changes nothing.
358	- **L2 ADAPT.** Settings are stored as numbered versions, and every decision records which version it used. A future learning layer will propose a new "learned" version, never edit silently, so every change is visible and reversible.
359	- **RECORD.** Every person gets a decision row for every hour, with an outcome (sent, held, suppressed or no event), a reason code and a stage-by-stage trace of the inputs, values and results. "Why didn't I hear about it at 2am?" always has an answer, as complete as "why did I hear about it?"
360	- **REPLAY.** Nothing in the pipeline reads the real clock, and every hour is recomputed from the readings known at that moment. So replaying the past gives exactly the decisions the live system would have made. Replay is how the rules were tuned, and how caught versus missed moments are measured.
361	- **GUARD.** Not in the demo. At full scope it stands in front of every irreversible action: consent, confirmation and rate limits.
362	- **OPERATE.** Every ingestion run is logged with its freshness, failures and remaining rate limit, so the pipeline's own health is visible.
363	
364	---
365	
366	## 10. A night in Delhi, hour by hour (illustrative)
367	
368	The numbers are made up but follow the rules above. Arjun lives in Delhi and runs at 06:30. He has default sensitivity, quiet hours 22:00–07:00, and a check-in at 06:30.
369	
370	```
371	 local  band (NowCast)   station layer               Arjun's decision                         outcome
372	 -----  ---------------  --------------------------  ---------------------------------------  -------------------
373	 22:00  USG              normal for a Delhi night    no event                                 no event
374	 23:00  USG              rising                      climb needs 3 hours above the bar        no event
375	 00:00  USG              rising                      not yet                                  no event
376	 01:00  Unhealthy        CLIMB                       episode OPENS; worth it; pace, budget    held
377	                                                     ok; but quiet hours                      QUIET_HOURS_HELD
378	 02:00  Unhealthy        still climbing              same story, same band                    suppressed
379	                                                                                              DEDUP_SAME_BAND
380	 03:00  Unhealthy (peak) flat                        same story                               suppressed
381	 04:00  Unhealthy        easing                      same story                               suppressed
382	 06:30  Unhealthy        well above a usual morning  CHECK-IN wins over quiet hours; worse    SENT (one message)
383	                                                     than usual; the held message merges in
384	          "Air got worse overnight from about 1am and is still unhealthy, well above a normal
385	           Delhi morning. Maybe skip the outdoor run today and try an indoor workout."
386	 07:00  Unhealthy        -                           quiet hours end; nothing left to release  -
387	 10:00  Unhealthy        -                           same story, same band                     suppressed
388	 14:00  USG              calm hour 1                 episode RECOVERING                        no event
389	 17:00  USG              calm hour 4                 episode CLOSES; it lasted 16h, so worth   SENT
390	                                                     saying; 10.5h since last, pace ok
391	          "Delhi's air is back to its usual level after a rough 16 hours. If you missed your
392	           run this morning, the evening looks fine for it."
393	```
394	
395	Two messages in about 20 hours, each with context and one action. Every silent hour has a logged reason.
396	
397	---
398	
399	## 11. Decision record
400	
401	| # | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative | Industry lineage |
402	|---|---|---|---|---|
403	| 1 | One set of layers for both scopes; the demo uses stubs | the demo is the first slice of the product, not a throwaway | a demo-only script | — |
404	| 2 | Station scores are shared and never depend on the person | facts about a place are the same for everyone; personal bars move, scores don't | per-person detection | shared metrics, per-route rules (Prometheus, Alertmanager) |
405	| 3 | DECIDE split into per-story and per-person halves | the split is what prevents fatigue with many signals | one combined restraint step | incident handling (PagerDuty) + notification orchestration (Braze, Airship) |
406	| 4 | "Normal" per station **and** per hour of day, over 14 days | rush hours and nights differ; seasons drift | one average; fixed thresholds | seasonal anomaly baselines (Datadog) |
407	| 5 | Log scale with median and MAD | a doubling means the same everywhere; old spikes don't distort normal | mean and standard deviation | robust statistics |
408	| 6 | "Unusual" and "harmful" are separate scores | a clean city gets a lower bar without harmless alerts | one blended score | anomaly score + a published standard (EPA AQI) |
409	| 7 | EPA bands with NowCast | built for hourly use; one scale for every city | India's 24-hour index (too slow for hourly nudges) | US EPA / AirNow |
410	| 8 | Event shapes: spike, climb, elevated (+ clearing, floor), one label each | matches the brief's trend and spike; elevated catches slow build-ups | thresholds only | control charts: EWMA, CUSUM (NIST) |
411	| 9 | Episodes with hysteresis and a flap guard | one bad period is one story; no on-off-on storms | per-hour alerts with a mute timer | alert states and `for` (Prometheus, Grafana), dedup keys (PagerDuty) |
412	| 10 | Recompute every hour from stored data | replay equals live; late data handled for free | incremental detector state | backtesting |
413	| 11 | Hand-rolled decision pipeline | holding, pacing and episodes aren't covered by any rule library | rule-engine, CEL, ZEN, durable_rules | — |
414	| 12 | Hold overnight and release as one message | a dropped warning is a missed trigger | silences that discard | quiet hours (consumer apps) |
415	| 13 | Five cities, clean to dusty, one station each | shows per-city sensitivity; the brief counts cities | several stations per city | — |
416	| 14 | PM2.5 only in the demo | the only pollutant all five stations measure | multi-pollutant with gaps | — |
417	| 15 | Messages written by an LLM from verified facts, with a template fallback | natural wording without invented facts; works offline | free-form LLM; templates only | — |
418	| 16 | A 90-day sample ships in the repo | anyone can replay without an API key | live-only | — |
419	| 17 | A sensor silent for 24h closes its episode quietly, with no message | the story can't be finished honestly without data | telling the person the sensor went quiet | — |
420	| 18 | The morning check-in wins over quiet hours and absorbs held messages | the person chose that time to hear from us | quiet hours win | — |
421	| 19 | A late hour older than a person's last evaluated hour is scored, but doesn't rewind their story | re-running old hours would double-count episode changes; the score still shapes every later hour | re-evaluating history in place | — |
422	| 20 | The clock records "no data" only once the newest reading is over 3 hours old | normal publishing delay (0.5–2.5 h) isn't silence | marking every quiet tick as no data | — |
423	| 21 | One scheduler (APScheduler) runs both the live schedule and cron parsing for check-ins, also in replay | one source of truth for "when is 06:30 local" | a separate cron library | — |
424	
425	Decisions 17 and 18 were confirmed by Yashvi on 2026-10-18, and 19–21 with the implementation plan.
426

# How the agent decides

Status: **closed** · 2026-10-18 · This document is the design source of truth. Its decisions have been carried into [requirements.md](requirements.md), the specs ([S-A](specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md), [S-B](specs/S-B-rule-engine-research.md), [S-C](specs/S-C-rule-engine-spec.md)) and [QA.csv](QA.csv).

---

## 1. Purpose

The agent watches signals about a person's surroundings and body, decides on its own when something is worth knowing, and responds. It speaks rarely, says what changed and why it matters to *this* person, and offers one thing to do. Restraint matters as much as detection.

The design is described at two scopes that share **one set of layers**:

- **Full scope**, the ultimate goal: many signals (air, pollen, weather, heart rate, sleep, movement, the home) and many responses (a message, an alarm, a call for help, adjusting the home), with settings that learn.
- **Demo scope**, what we build now: air quality (PM2.5) in five cities, notifications only, every requirement in the brief met.

The demo isn't a separate, simpler design. It's the full design with some layers reduced to a single rule or left out. Sections 2–4 give the big picture. Sections 5–9 walk through the layers. Section 10 follows one night end to end, and section 11 records the decisions.

---

## 2. The layers at full scope

Eighteen layers in five planes. Each answers **one question** for **one unit of work**: a data source, a signal stream, a person, a story (episode) or a response.

```
 FULL SCOPE: the ultimate goal
 +================================================================================+
 | PLANE        UNIT OF WORK   LAYER          THE ONE QUESTION IT ANSWERS         |
 +================================================================================+
 | SENSE        per source     S1 INGEST      Did we get the data?                 |
 |                             S2 VALIDATE    Can we trust it?                     |
 |                             S3 RESOLVE     Whose is it, where does it apply,    |
 |                                            and may we use it? (consent)         |
 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | UNDERSTAND   per stream     U1 LEARN       What is normal for this stream,      |
 |                                            here, at this time?                  |
 |                             U2 SCORE       How unusual? How harmful?            |
 |              per person     U3 FUSE        What does it mean alongside their    |
 |                                            other signals and context?           |
 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | DECIDE       per story      D1 TRIGGER     Is this an event for this person,    |
 |                                            and what kind?                       |
 |                             D2 EPISODE     A new story, or the same story?      |
 |                             D3 WORTH IT    Is there anything new in this story? |
 |                             D4 PACE        Too soon since this story last spoke?|
 |              per person     D5 ARBITRATE   Which candidate wins right now?      |
 |                             D6 RESPOND     Tell them, set an alarm, call for    |
 |                                            help, or adjust the home?            |
 |                             D7 BUDGET      Can we afford their attention today? |
 |                             D8 TIMING      Is now the right moment?             |
 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | ACT          per response   A1 COMPOSE     How do we say it?                    |
 |                             A2 DELIVER     Did it reach them / did it happen?   |
 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | LEARN        per person     L1 FEEDBACK    How did they respond?                |
 |                             L2 ADAPT       Should their settings change?        |
 +================================================================================+
 | CROSS-CUTTING  RECORD   every answer, including "stay quiet"                    |
 |                REPLAY   any past hour, exactly as it was known then             |
 |                GUARD    consent, and safety limits on high-stakes actions       |
 |                OPERATE  is the pipeline itself healthy (freshness, failures)?   |
 +================================================================================+
```

Three structural choices shape everything else:

- **Station work is shared, person work is not.** SENSE and UNDERSTAND produce facts about a place that are the same for everyone: how unusual the air is, and how harmful. Everything personal (sensitivity, schedule, history) starts at D1. A person's settings never change a station's scores.
- **DECIDE has two halves.** D1–D4 judge **one story at a time** ("Delhi's air is getting worse"). D5–D8 judge **the person as a whole**, across every story competing for their attention: Delhi air, high pollen, an odd heart-rate reading. Keeping those apart is what stops alert fatigue once there are many signals.
- **What comes before when.** D6 RESPOND comes before D7 BUDGET and D8 TIMING, because the kind of response changes both. A call for help ignores quiet hours and is never "over budget". A routine heads-up respects both.

What full scope looks like in practice (illustrative):

```
  Fusion: three ordinary-looking signals become one clear message

   air (U2):    PM2.5 above normal, Unhealthy ----+
   body (U2):   heart rate 15% above their usual -+--> U3 FUSE: "exerting in bad air"
   motion (S1): running for the last 20 min ------+          |
                                                             v
                       D1..D8 --> A1: "The air's turned unhealthy and your heart rate's
                                       up. Maybe walk the rest of the way home."

  High-stakes response: GUARD sits in front of every irreversible action

   asthma profile + Hazardous air + no reply to 2 messages in 30 min
       --> D6 RESPOND proposes "SOS to emergency contact"
       --> GUARD: is consent on file? Is the action rate-limited? Does it need a
                  one-tap confirmation, or a timeout?
       --> A2 DELIVER: send it, and record the receipt
```

---

## 3. The layers at demo scope

The same eighteen layers. Each one is **REAL** (built properly), a **STUB** (a single rule, named in code and in every decision trace, so the seam is visible) or **NONE** (left out, because nothing needs it yet).

```
 DEMO SCOPE: air quality, 5 cities, notifications only
 +==================================================================================+
 | LAYER          STATUS  WHAT IT IS IN THE DEMO                          BRIEF      |
 +==================================================================================+
 | S1 INGEST      REAL    OpenAQ hourly, trailing 24h window, backfill   B1         |
 | S2 VALIDATE    REAL    invalid / low coverage / stuck / glitch checks B2d        |
 | S3 RESOLVE     STUB    hardcoded user -> one station; no consent step  B5         |
 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | U1 LEARN       REAL    14-day hour-of-day baseline per station         B2e, B5    |
 | U2 SCORE       REAL    unusual: z, EWMA, CUSUM, slope                  B2e        |
 |                        harmful: NowCast -> EPA band                               |
 | U3 FUSE        NONE    one signal, so nothing to fuse                  -          |
 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | D1 TRIGGER     REAL    spike / climb / elevated / clearing / floor,    B2a-c, B5  |
 |                        scaled by the person's sensitivity                         |
 | D2 EPISODE     REAL    lifecycle, hysteresis, flap guard, timeout      B3         |
 | D3 WORTH IT    REAL    relevance floor, one-band escalation,           B3         |
 |                        "cleared" only after a bad period                          |
 | D4 PACE        REAL    6h gap, doubling within a story                 BX1        |
 | D5 ARBITRATE   STUB    one message per person per hour, by priority    B3         |
 | D6 RESPOND     STUB    always "notify"                                 -          |
 | D7 BUDGET      STUB    at most 3 non-severe messages per person a day  B3         |
 | D8 TIMING      REAL    quiet hours (hold and release), morning check-in -         |
 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | A1 COMPOSE     REAL    LLM from verified facts, template fallback      B4         |
 | A2 DELIVER     STUB    "delivered" = visible in the feed and export    S5         |
 +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | L1 FEEDBACK    REAL*   records acted / dismissed / not useful          -          |
 | L2 ADAPT       STUB    no changes; rules are versioned for later       -          |
 +==================================================================================+
 | RECORD  REAL   decision log for every person x hour, with reasons      B6         |
 | REPLAY  REAL   replay harness on as-known data, caught vs missed       BX2        |
 | GUARD   NONE   no high-stakes actions yet                              -          |
 | OPERATE REAL*  ingestion runs: freshness, failures, rate limits        -          |
 +==================================================================================+
   REAL* = real but minimal.   11 real · 6 stubs · 1 none, plus 3 of 4 cross-cutting.
```

How each stub or empty layer grows into its full form:

| Layer | Demo | Full scope |
|---|---|---|
| S3 RESOLVE | a fixed person-to-station mapping | identity, devices, locations, consent per signal |
| U3 FUSE | none | combines streams and context into one meaning ("exerting in bad air") |
| D5 ARBITRATE | one message per hour, by a fixed priority | ranks competing stories by urgency and relevance |
| D6 RESPOND | always notify | chooses between a message, an alarm, an SOS, a home action, with escalation |
| D7 BUDGET | 3 non-severe a day | an attention budget shared by all signals, tuned per person |
| A2 DELIVER | written to the feed | push, email, SMS, device APIs, with retries and receipts |
| L2 ADAPT | none; rules are versioned | proposes a new "learned" rules version, bounded by GUARD and reversible |
| GUARD | none | consent, confirmations and rate limits before any irreversible action |

A stub costs one rule, but it puts the layer in the code and in every trace (`ARBITRATE: 1 candidate, kept`). Later, the layer gets filled in, not invented. Three stubs are needed even in the demo. A check-in and an episode message can land in the same hour (ARBITRATE). A jumpy day with back-to-back episodes could otherwise stack up messages (BUDGET). And the brief asks for a notification history (DELIVER).

---

## 4. Two clocks drive it

Most work happens when new data arrives. Some must happen when **no** data arrives: noticing a silent sensor, releasing messages held overnight, running the morning check-in. So every hour, every person gets a decision, whichever clock fired.

```
   OpenAQ
     |   every hour at :20, fetch the last 24h per sensor
     v
  [S1..S2] --new or revised hours--> [U1..U2] --scores--> [D1..D8] --> [A1..A2] --> feed
                                                              ^
   CLOCK -----------------------------------------------------+
     every hour, plus each person's check-in time and the end of their quiet hours:
       - marks sensors without fresh data as NO_DATA
       - releases messages held overnight
       - runs the morning check-in
```

---

## 5. Sense: getting data we can trust

**S1 INGEST.** Every hour, for each tracked sensor, fetch the **last 24 hours** and store anything new. Data usually arrives 0.5–2.5 hours late, and sometimes much later. The overlapping window picks up late readings, and the newly filled hours are evaluated as if they had arrived on time. Readings are never overwritten. A changed value is stored as a new version with the time we received it, so we can always ask "what did we know at 3am?". On first run, up to 90 days are backfilled so a baseline exists from day one.

**S2 VALIDATE.** OpenAQ doesn't flag bad readings, so we do.

| Check | Rule | Example from the real data |
|---|---|---|
| Invalid | below 0 or above 1000 µg/m³ | Sydney low-cost sensors: about a third of hours ≤ 0 (not tracked) |
| Low coverage | the hour is less than 75% complete | — |
| Stuck | the same value for 6+ hours | — |
| Glitch | 3× higher than both neighbours and +20 µg/m³ | Mumbai: 75 → **980** → 90 in three hours; 8 such hours in 58 days, none flagged by OpenAQ |

Excluded readings stay visible as evidence. They just don't count. The newest hour can't be glitch-checked until the next one arrives. That costs nothing, because a spike needs two hours of confirmation anyway.

**S3 RESOLVE.** In the demo, each person follows exactly one station. At full scope this layer answers whose device a reading came from, which places a person cares about, and whether we have consent to use each signal.

---

## 6. Understand: what is normal, and what is harmful

**U1 LEARN.** For each station and each hour of the day, the agent learns what's normal from the last 14 days. It works on a log scale, so a doubling means the same thing in Helsinki and in Delhi. It uses the median and median absolute deviation, so last week's smoke doesn't distort "normal". Hours with little history borrow from the station's all-day pattern, and a station needs 72 hours of clean history before it can judge anything. Each station also gets a **typical band**: the official air quality category of its usual level.

```
  what "normal" looks like (90-day medians, µg/m³)

   Helsinki     4.2  |##                                     typical: Good
   Los Angeles 10.0  |#####                                  typical: Moderate
   Bengaluru   20.7  |##########                             typical: Moderate
   Dubai       41.0  |####################                   typical: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups
   Delhi       45.9  |######################                 typical: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups
                     +----+----+----+----+----+
                     0   10   20   30   40   50
```

**U2 SCORE.** Two different questions get two different answers, and neither depends on who is asking.
- **How unusual?** How far the latest hour sits from normal for that hour of day (z). That comes with a smoothed version (EWMA), a running total of excess (CUSUM) and the direction of the last 6 hours (slope).
- **How harmful?** The official US EPA category of the hourly-weighted average (NowCast): Good, Moderate, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, Hazardous. Same scale everywhere.

A message needs the right combination of the two:

```
                              Is it HARMFUL? (EPA band, same scale everywhere)
                               no (Good)                   yes (Moderate or worse)
                         +---------------------------+---------------------------------+
   Is it UNUSUAL         | Stay quiet.               | TELL THEM.                       |
   for this place?   yes | "Helsinki went 3 -> 5."   | "Worse than a normal Delhi       |
   (learned per          | Odd, but harmless.        |  morning, and unhealthy."        |
   station, per hour)    |                           |                                  |
                         +---------------------------+---------------------------------+
                      no | Nothing to say.           | Mostly quiet. Delhi sits in      |
                         |                           | "unhealthy for sensitive groups" |
                         |                           | for weeks; saying so hourly is   |
                         |                           | noise. Two exceptions:           |
                         |                           | - crossing UP into the person's  |
                         |                           |   alert band                     |
                         |                           | - the morning check-in, when     |
                         |                           |   today is worse than usual      |
                         +---------------------------+---------------------------------+
```

That's how a clean city gets a lower bar for "unusual" without anyone hearing about harmless changes.

**U3 FUSE** is not in the demo. At full scope it combines a person's streams and context into one meaning before anything is decided.

---

## 7. Decide: from a score to a message, with restraint

### 7.1 D1 TRIGGER: is it an event, and what kind?

```
  how far above normal (z)
   ^
   |        SPIKE                 CLIMB                    ELEVATED
   |          |                       ___/
   |          |\                  ___/                   ______________
   |          | \            ____/                  ____/
   |   _______|  \______  __/                    __/
   |
   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------> hours
      a sharp jump vs the      rising, hour after        stuck above normal
      last few hours           hour                      for many hours, but
                                                         not rising
      far above normal in      smoothed level above      running total of excess
      2 of the last 3 hours    the bar for 3 hours       crosses the bar; resets
                               AND the 6h slope is up    once it fires

      CLEARING   an open episode has 4 calm hours AND is back to the station's typical band
      FLOOR      crossing UP into the person's alert band, whatever is "normal" there
```

- **One label per event**, by priority: spike, then climb, then elevated. The label drives the wording ("jumped sharply", "getting worse since 2am", "stuck above normal all day").
- **Every way of getting worse is covered.** Air goes up fast (spike), keeps rising (climb), or sits high and flat (elevated). Falling-but-still-high isn't a new event. It's the same story continuing.
- **Elevated exists to catch what the others miss.** These are slow build-ups that never look dramatic in any single hour.
- **The person's sensitivity scales every bar.** Sensitive people get bars 25% lower; people who want fewer messages get bars 25% higher. Station scores are unchanged; only the bar moves.

### 7.2 D2 EPISODE: one bad period is one story

```
                 event fires AND the air is at least Moderate
     NORMAL  --------------------------------------------->  ACTIVE  <-----+
       ^                                                        |          |
       |                                            a calm hour |          | event again, or
       |  6h pass after close                                   v          | a non-calm hour
       |                                                   RECOVERING -----+
     CLOSED  <------------- 4 calm hours in a row --------------+
       |   ^
       |   +---- 24h with NO DATA: close quietly, no message (NO_DATA_TIMEOUT)
       |
       +-- event within 6h of closing --> the SAME episode reopens (no "it's getting bad" again)

     NO DATA (under 24h): the episode is frozen. Nothing opens, closes or notifies.
                          When data returns, the missing hours are replayed in order.
```

### 7.3 D3–D8: restraint, story first, then person

```
   candidate (opened / got worse / cleared / check-in)
        |
   ---- per STORY -------------------------------------------------------------------
        v
   [D3 WORTH IT]   anything NEW in this story?
        |            opened: yes, if the air is at least Moderate
        |            got worse: only if a full band worse than last told
        |            cleared: only after a genuinely bad period
        |                     (12h or longer, or peaked above both USG and the usual band)
        |   no --> suppressed  BELOW_RELEVANCE / DEDUP_SAME_BAND / RECOVERY_NOT_WORTH_SAYING
        v
   [D4 PACE]       too soon since this story last spoke?   6h, then 12h, then 24h
        |   no --> suppressed  COOLDOWN                  (severe air skips the wait)
        |
   ---- per PERSON ------------------------------------------------------------------
        v
   [D5 ARBITRATE]  several candidates this hour? keep one:
        |            got worse > opened > cleared > check-in
        |   lost --> suppressed  ARBITRATED_OUT
        v
   [D6 RESPOND]    which response?   (demo: always notify)
        v
   [D7 BUDGET]     over today's attention budget?   3 non-severe a day
        |   yes --> suppressed  DAILY_BUDGET          (severe air is never over budget)
        v
   [D8 TIMING]     a good moment?
        |            quiet hours (22:00-07:00 by default) hold messages until morning,
        |            unless the air is Very Unhealthy or worse
        |            the morning check-in is an explicit "talk to me now": it wins over
        |            quiet hours and absorbs any held messages into one
        |   no --> held  QUIET_HOURS_HELD   (released later as ONE combined message)
        v
   [A1 COMPOSE] -> [A2 DELIVER] -> sent
```

- **PACE and BUDGET are different questions.** PACE asks "too soon *in this story*?" and resets when the story ends. BUDGET asks "how much of *this person's* attention have we spent today, across every story?" With one signal they rarely disagree. With several, three well-paced stories can still add up to too much.
- **Held messages are never just dropped.** At release, everything held for a person becomes **one** message about the current state. It's re-checked against D3–D7 at that moment. If the story ended overnight without ever being told, nothing is sent.
- **The check-in is not a daily report.** At the person's chosen time, it looks at the last 8 hours. It speaks only if the air is at least Moderate and worse than usual for that time, and nothing was sent in the last 6 hours.

**How the numbers were chosen.** Every bar and waiting time above was tuned by replaying 90 days of real data from all five cities. On the earlier version of these rules, a default person got about 1.5 messages a week in Helsinki, 2–2.5 in Los Angeles, Bengaluru and Dubai, and 3.5 in Delhi during its build-up season. The replay harness re-measures this whenever a rule changes.

---

## 8. Act: saying it well

**A1 COMPOSE.** The decision layers hand over **verified facts**, never raw data:

```
  { kind: "got worse",  city: "Delhi",  local time: 08:00,
    now: 142 µg/m³, Very Unhealthy,      usual for 8am: 48, USG,
    story: since 2am, 6 hours, peak 151 at 6am,
    history: "worst since 13 Oct", "third bad morning this week",
    person: Arjun, runs at 06:30,
    action options: skip the outdoor run | keep windows closed | wear an N95 outside }
```

- An LLM writes one or two sentences from these facts. A validator then checks the result: short enough for a phone notification, includes exactly one of the offered actions, and cites no number or date that isn't in the facts.
- If the LLM fails the check or isn't available, a template writes the message from the same facts.
- Past context is always included for climb, spike and clearing messages ("since 2am", "worst since Tuesday", "back to normal after two rough days"). It's never a bare status like "AQI is now 142".

**A2 DELIVER.** In the demo, a message is "delivered" when it appears in the person's feed and in the exported history. Real channels come at full scope.

---

## 9. Learn, and what runs across everything

- **L1 FEEDBACK.** A person can mark a message as acted on, dismissed or not useful. In the demo, this is stored and shown next to the decision, and changes nothing.
- **L2 ADAPT.** Settings are stored as numbered versions, and every decision records which version it used. A future learning layer will propose a new "learned" version, never edit silently, so every change is visible and reversible.
- **RECORD.** Every person gets a decision row for every hour, with an outcome (sent, held, suppressed or no event), a reason code and a stage-by-stage trace of the inputs, values and results. "Why didn't I hear about it at 2am?" always has an answer, as complete as "why did I hear about it?"
- **REPLAY.** Nothing in the pipeline reads the real clock, and every hour is recomputed from the readings known at that moment. So replaying the past gives exactly the decisions the live system would have made. Replay is how the rules were tuned, and how caught versus missed moments are measured.
- **GUARD.** Not in the demo. At full scope it stands in front of every irreversible action: consent, confirmation and rate limits.
- **OPERATE.** Every ingestion run is logged with its freshness, failures and remaining rate limit, so the pipeline's own health is visible.

---

## 10. A night in Delhi, hour by hour (illustrative)

The numbers are made up but follow the rules above. Arjun lives in Delhi and runs at 06:30. He has default sensitivity, quiet hours 22:00–07:00, and a check-in at 06:30.

```
 local  band (NowCast)   station layer               Arjun's decision                         outcome
 -----  ---------------  --------------------------  ---------------------------------------  -------------------
 22:00  USG              normal for a Delhi night    no event                                 no event
 23:00  USG              rising                      climb needs 3 hours above the bar        no event
 00:00  USG              rising                      not yet                                  no event
 01:00  Unhealthy        CLIMB                       episode OPENS; worth it; pace, budget    held
                                                     ok; but quiet hours                      QUIET_HOURS_HELD
 02:00  Unhealthy        still climbing              same story, same band                    suppressed
                                                                                              DEDUP_SAME_BAND
 03:00  Unhealthy (peak) flat                        same story                               suppressed
 04:00  Unhealthy        easing                      same story                               suppressed
 06:30  Unhealthy        well above a usual morning  CHECK-IN wins over quiet hours; worse    SENT (one message)
                                                     than usual; the held message merges in
          "Air got worse overnight from about 1am and is still unhealthy, well above a normal
           Delhi morning. Maybe skip the outdoor run today and try an indoor workout."
 07:00  Unhealthy        -                           quiet hours end; nothing left to release  -
 10:00  Unhealthy        -                           same story, same band                     suppressed
 14:00  USG              calm hour 1                 episode RECOVERING                        no event
 17:00  USG              calm hour 4                 episode CLOSES; it lasted 16h, so worth   SENT
                                                     saying; 10.5h since last, pace ok

```

Two messages in about 20 hours, each with context and one action. Every silent hour has a logged reason.

---

## 11. Decision record

| # | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative | Industry lineage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One set of layers for both scopes; the demo uses stubs | the demo is the first slice of the product, not a throwaway | a demo-only script | — |
| 2 | Station scores are shared and never depend on the person | facts about a place are the same for everyone; personal bars move, scores don't | per-person detection | shared metrics, per-route rules (Prometheus, Alertmanager) |
| 3 | DECIDE split into per-story and per-person halves | the split is what prevents fatigue with many signals | one combined restraint step | incident handling (PagerDuty) + notification orchestration (Braze, Airship) |
| 4 | "Normal" per station **and** per hour of day, over 14 days | rush hours and nights differ; seasons drift | one average; fixed thresholds | seasonal anomaly baselines (Datadog) |
| 5 | Log scale with median and MAD | a doubling means the same everywhere; old spikes don't distort normal | mean and standard deviation | robust statistics |
| 6 | "Unusual" and "harmful" are separate scores | a clean city gets a lower bar without harmless alerts | one blended score | anomaly score + a published standard (EPA AQI) |
| 7 | EPA bands with NowCast | built for hourly use; one scale for every city | India's 24-hour index (too slow for hourly nudges) | US EPA / AirNow |
| 8 | Event shapes: spike, climb, elevated (+ clearing, floor), one label each | matches the brief's trend and spike; elevated catches slow build-ups | thresholds only | control charts: EWMA, CUSUM (NIST) |
| 9 | Episodes with hysteresis and a flap guard | one bad period is one story; no on-off-on storms | per-hour alerts with a mute timer | alert states and `for` (Prometheus, Grafana), dedup keys (PagerDuty) |
| 10 | Recompute every hour from stored data | replay equals live; late data handled for free | incremental detector state | backtesting |
| 11 | Hand-rolled decision pipeline | holding, pacing and episodes aren't covered by any rule library | rule-engine, CEL, ZEN, durable_rules | — |
| 12 | Hold overnight and release as one message | a dropped warning is a missed trigger | silences that discard | quiet hours (consumer apps) |
| 13 | Five cities, clean to dusty, one station each | shows per-city sensitivity; the brief counts cities | several stations per city | — |
| 14 | PM2.5 only in the demo | the only pollutant all five stations measure | multi-pollutant with gaps | — |
| 15 | Messages written by an LLM from verified facts, with a template fallback | natural wording without invented facts; works offline | free-form LLM; templates only | — |
| 16 | A 90-day sample ships in the repo | anyone can replay without an API key | live-only | — |
| 17 | A sensor silent for 24h closes its episode quietly, with no message | the story can't be finished honestly without data | telling the person the sensor went quiet | — |
| 18 | The morning check-in wins over quiet hours and absorbs held messages | the person chose that time to hear from us | quiet hours win | — |
| 19 | A late hour older than a person's last evaluated hour is scored, but doesn't rewind their story | re-running old hours would double-count episode changes; the score still shapes every later hour | re-evaluating history in place | — |
| 20 | The clock records "no data" only once the newest reading is over 3 hours old | normal publishing delay (0.5–2.5 h) isn't silence | marking every quiet tick as no data | — |
| 21 | One scheduler (APScheduler) runs both the live schedule and cron parsing for check-ins, also in replay | one source of truth for "when is 06:30 local" | a separate cron library | — |

Decisions 17 and 18 were confirmed by Yashvi on 2026-10-18, and 19–21 with the implementation plan.

# Requirements — Proactive Health Insight Agent

Status: approved · updated 2026-10-18 from the closed [explainer](explainer.md) · Owner: Yashvi Bansal

This document turns the Orange Invest take-home brief ("Proactive Air Quality Insight Agent") into a product vision plus a v1 scope. Every requirement in the brief has an ID here and a row in the traceability table (section 9), so nothing gets missed. Detailed specs are listed in section 10.

The design behind these requirements, with diagrams of every layer, is in [explainer.md](explainer.md), the design source of truth. This document is the **spec**: what to build and why. **How each requirement is verified** lives in [QA.csv](QA.csv): one row per test case, with `requirement_ids` tracing back to the IDs here and the brief (B1–B6, BX1–2, S1–5). Every requirement ID in this document has at least one test case. When a requirement changes, update its rows in QA.csv in the same change.

---

## 1. Why this exists

People care about their environment and health signals, but they don't want to check a number every hour. They want something that watches for them and speaks up, unprompted, only when it's actually worth knowing. It should say what changed, why it matters to them, and the one thing to do about it.

The measure of success is restraint as much as detection. A nudge that's late, wrong, or repeated costs trust. A system that stays quiet when nothing has meaningfully changed earns it.

### What this submission should demonstrate

Two things at once, and the requirements are organised to show both:

- **Systems thinking with a long horizon.** The ultimate product (section 2) is much broader than air quality. v1 is built on seams (section 4), so new signals, triggers and actions slot in without a rewrite.
- **Tactical agility.** v1 ships every requirement in the brief, each with exactly one real implementation behind each seam. Nothing is built speculatively.

---

## 2. Ultimate goal (long-term vision)

A proactive personal health agent that watches signals about a person's environment and body, decides on its own when something matters, and acts on it, from a simple heads-up up to taking an action on their behalf.

| Dimension | v1 | Later |
|---|---|---|
| **Signals: external** | Air quality (OpenAQ) | Pollen, UV, heat index, weather |
| **Signals: internal** | none | Heart rate, sleep, activity from wearables |
| **Triggers / rule inputs** | Schedule (cron-style), geo-location, air quality parameters | Movement (gyroscope/accelerometer), home systems (purifier, thermostat, sensors) |
| **Actions** | Notification | Set an alarm, send SOS emails to contacts, control home devices |
| **Configuration** | Smart defaults ("on its own" criteria), tunable per user | Self-learning adjustments based on how the user responds |

---

## 3. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals

### Goals (v1)
- G1. Meet every core requirement in the brief, traceably.
- G2. Detection that is learned from each station's own history, not fixed thresholds.
- G3. Notifications a real person would want to get: rare, specific, contextual, actionable.
- G4. Every decision, including the decision *not* to notify, is explainable after the fact.
- G5. Clear extension seams so the long-term vision reads as a credible next step, not a slide.

### Non-goals (v1)
- Internal health signals, non-notification actions, movement/home triggers.
- Self-learning config adjustments (v1 only *records* user responses; see FR-FB).
- Polished frontend, authentication, multi-tenancy (brief explicitly excludes these).
- Real push delivery infrastructure (APNs/FCM) or any external channel; v1 notifications are stored, served by API and exported (section 8).

### Anti-goals (would be a failure even if it technically works)
- A v1 stuffed with half-built plugin frameworks, registries, or abstractions with one caller each "for the future". That undercuts the agility story.
- A clever single script with no path forward. That undercuts the systems story.
- Notifications that read like status reports ("AQI is now 142") or templates with numbers swapped in.
- A detector that is a fixed threshold dressed up as a model.
- Nagging: repeated, near-identical messages about the same episode.

---

## 4. System shape and extension seams

The system is eighteen layers in five planes, the same at full scope and in v1. They're explained, with diagrams, in [explainer.md](explainer.md) §2–3.

```
 SENSE       S1 Ingest · S2 Validate · S3 Resolve                         per source
 UNDERSTAND  U1 Learn · U2 Score · U3 Fuse                                per stream / person
 DECIDE      D1 Trigger · D2 Episode · D3 Worth it · D4 Pace              per story
             D5 Arbitrate · D6 Respond · D7 Budget · D8 Timing            per person
 ACT         A1 Compose · A2 Deliver                                      per response
 LEARN       L1 Feedback · L2 Adapt                                       per person
 ACROSS      Record · Replay · Guard · Operate
```

In v1, each layer is either **real**, a **stub** (a single named rule, visible in every decision trace) or **none**:
- Real: S1, S2, U1, U2, D1–D4, D8, A1, L1 (minimal).
- Stubs: S3, D5, D6, D7, A2, L2.

## 5. Users, cities and how they configure

- **Cities/stations:** 4–5 distinct cities (the brief counts cities, so never two stations in one city), each with one primary OpenAQ station, deliberately mixed between low-pollution and naturally high-pollution or dusty regions, so baseline sensitivity (FR-SENS) is visibly exercised. Final picks depend on data availability (spec S-A).
- **Users:** a few hardcoded users per city with different sensitivities and habits (e.g. an asthmatic morning runner in a clean city vs. a commuter in a dusty one). No auth.
- **Configuration:** via config file and/or API. No settings UI is required. Every user works correctly with zero configuration, on default "on its own" criteria.

---

## 8. Constraints and decisions so far

| Decision | Made by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Core service in Python | Yashvi | FastAPI likely (matches the JD's named stack); final in the design |
| Optional Next.js demo UI on Vercel | Yashvi | Concept demo only |
| v1 signal = air quality only, via OpenAQ | Yashvi / brief | OpenAQ v3 requires a free API key |
| v1 action = notification only | Yashvi | |
| v1 rule inputs = schedule, geo, air quality params, with defaults | Yashvi | |
| Schedule rule = quiet hours + optional daily check-in | Yashvi (confirmed proposal) | |
| Self-learning = record feedback only in v1 | Proposed by Claude | Confirm in review |
| Rules are filters/dials on a learned detector, never a replacement | Proposed by Claude | Needed to satisfy B2's "learned model" requirement |
| Config via file/API, no settings UI | Proposed by Claude | Brief excludes frontend |
| Deadline: built within the current working session | Yashvi | Drives the cut order below |
| Cut order if time runs short: Next.js demo first, then the daily check-in, then cooldown decay. The replay harness stays | Proposed by Claude, accepted | The harness is the proof that detection works |
| Hosting: one small hosted Python process that really polls hourly, plus a managed database. No queue or Redis in v1 | Proposed by Claude, accepted | Live history for the demo; anti-goal on premature infra |
| A recorded OpenAQ data sample ships in the repo so replay runs without an API key | Proposed by Claude, accepted | Reviewers can run it cold |
| Daily check-in uses no forecast: overnight levels and the current trend vs. the station's normal for that hour | Proposed by Claude, accepted | Forecasts become a later signal source |
| v1 delivery = notifications stored, served by API and exported as history. No external channel | Claude's call | Resolves Q1; email/Telegram is a later action |
| One location per user in v1; the rule format allows a list | Claude's call | Resolves Q2 |
| Severe events break through quiet hours | Claude's call | Resolves Q3; "severe" defined in S-C |
| 4–5 distinct cities, one primary station each | Claude's call | Brief counts cities |
| Readings carry measured and ingested timestamps; replay is "as known" | Claude's call | Makes replay faithful to live; small schema cost |
| Missed-trigger handling is live (elevated build-ups, late data, gaps, clock tick), not only via the harness | Claude's call | B2d is core; the harness is a bonus |
| Eighteen-layer model, same at full scope and in v1; v1 uses stubs, not shortcuts | Proposed by Claude, accepted | [explainer.md](explainer.md) §2–3 |
| Station scores are shared and never depend on the user | Proposed by Claude, accepted | explainer §2; FR-SENS-4 |
| Event kinds are spike / climb / elevated (+ clearing, floor), one label each; climb must be rising | Proposed by Claude, accepted | Audit: 53% of the old "trend" hours were flat or falling |
| Arbitration and attention budget are separate layers from cooldown | Proposed by Claude, accepted | They differ by scope: per person vs per episode |
| A clock tick evaluates every user hourly, even with no new data | Proposed by Claude, accepted | FR-CLK-1 |
| A sensor silent for 24h closes its episode quietly, without telling the user | Yashvi | FR-DEDUP-8 |
| The morning check-in wins over quiet hours and absorbs held notices | Yashvi | FR-RULE-2 |
